= Cloud November 6, 2026

[NOTE]
====
Cloud release notes are typically published weekly and summarize changes since the previous publication. === Analytics reports

- Fixed an issue where exporting the *Device Utilization*, *Parallel Sessions*, and *Sessions per Day* reports as CSV or PNG returned no data. The CSV showed an export error in place of the report data.
- CSV exports of *Parallel Sessions* and *Sessions per Day* list one row per day in date order. CSV exports of *Device Utilization* sort by *Sessions*, with the most-used devices at the top.
- PNG exports of *Parallel Sessions* and *Sessions per Day* now include the report's chart as a bar chart. Previously, the PNG showed only the report title for these reports.
- Exports use the date range selected for the report, or the report's saved date range when none is selected.

== Kobiton API: session updates take effect immediately

- Updates to a session's name, description, or state through `PUT /v2/sessions/{id}` now take effect before the request returns. After the request returns HTTP 200, `GET /v2/sessions/{id}` returns the new name, description, and state right away. Previously, the change could take 30 seconds or longer to appear.
- A `PASSED` or `FAILED` state takes effect immediately only for a session that has ended. Session lists, search, and reports show the new state without additional delay.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55961): Jira lists fix version 2026.11.06 and states the change works on Cloud and
// Standalone. Confirm the target release-notes page or pages for this entry.

// Source: KOB-55770

== Device passcodes returned to every org member in the v2 devices API

`GET /v2/devices` and `GET /v2/devices/udid/{deviceUdid}` now return a device's `passcode` to every user who can access the device. Previously, only users with the ADMIN role received this field.

* The `has_passcode` and `passcode_enabled` fields are unchanged.
* The v1 device endpoints are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-52861 | Escalation | Component: Device Tags | Fix version: 2026.11.04.
// Jira status: Released. Production verification passed 2026-11-04.

== Device tags API

- Fixed an issue where adding a tag to a device through the API could fail with HTTP 400 and a `SequelizeUniqueConstraintError` message.
- Adding a tag that is already assigned to a device now succeeds instead of returning an error.
- When several requests add the same tag to the same device at the same time, every request succeeds and the tag is assigned to the device only once.
- The fix applies to these device-tag endpoints:
** `POST /v1/tags/device/\{udid}`
** `POST /v1/tags/assign`
** `POST /v2/tags/\{tagName}/devices`
** `POST /v2/tags/devices`

=== Web views available in iOS Appium sessions

Fixed an issue where Appium automation sessions on iOS devices could intermittently return only the `NATIVE_APP` context. In affected sessions, web content opened in the app, such as a sign-in page, did not appear as a `WEBVIEW` context and could not be inspected or automated. Web views are now available as a `WEBVIEW` context in these sessions.

Web views on iOS devices still require *Web Inspector* to be turned on in *Settings → Safari → Advanced*.

// Source: KOB-52358

== Appium device selection requires only platformName

Fixed an issue where Appium sessions failed with `deviceTags is required` when the request didn't include `deviceName`, `udid`, or `kobiton:deviceTags`. The error appeared even when `kobiton:deviceTags` was omitted entirely.

* When `udid` isn't provided, `platformName` is the only required device-selection capability. `deviceName` and `kobiton:deviceTags` are optional filters.
* If neither `deviceName` nor `kobiton:deviceTags` is provided, the session runs on any available device that matches `platformName` and your other capabilities in the requested device group. The default device group is `ANY`, which includes your organization's devices and Kobiton cloud devices.
* An empty `kobiton:deviceTags` value is ignored.
* If neither `udid` nor `platformName` is provided, session creation fails with `platformName is required`.
* Appium Turbo Test sessions that don't include `udid`, `device_name`, or `device_tags` now fail with `one of udid, device_name or device_tags is required`.

// Source: KOB-55749 from PR #864
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/864

== Session timeout now ends Turbo Test sessions

Turbo Test sessions now end when the session timeout (`session_timeout`) is reached. Previously, a test script that ran past the session timeout kept the session running and the device in use until the script finished on its own.

- When the session timeout is reached, Kobiton stops the test script and every process it started, ends the session, and releases the device.
- If the script does not start its session before the timeout, the run fails with a message stating that the script did not finish within the session timeout.
- Scripts that finish before the session timeout run as before.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55749): The `session_timeout` request parameter is not listed in the Request parameter reference in automation-testing:turbo-test-execution/run-appium-test.adoc. Confirm whether to keep the parameter name here, and its unit and default, before publishing.

// Source: KOB-54409

== Support for the MCP 2026-07-28 specification

The Kobiton MCP server now supports the MCP 2026-07-28 specification. AI clients that use the new protocol connect without an initialization handshake, and clients that use earlier MCP versions continue to work without changes.

* AI clients on the 2026-07-28 protocol, such as current versions of Claude Code, connect statelessly and can use server discovery and cacheable tool lists.
* AI clients on earlier MCP versions connect as before. No reconnection or configuration change is required.
* Requests from untrusted browser origins are rejected, which protects the MCP endpoint against DNS rebinding attacks.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54409): Confirm whether customers need to know which browser origins are trusted by default, and whether Standalone customers can change the trusted origins. The source states only that untrusted origins are rejected.

=== iPad Inspector fix

- Fixed an issue where *Session Explorer Inspector* showed the same XML hierarchy for every step of an iPad automation session started without an app, such as a web session in Safari. *Session Explorer Inspector* now shows the hierarchy for each step of these sessions, as it already does on iPhone and Android devices. iPad automation sessions that install an app, and manual sessions on iPad, are unchanged.

== Passcode indicator for Android devices

The device list passcode indicator now covers Android devices, and the *Passcode* filter uses clearer labels.

- Android devices with a passcode now display the passcode icon in card view and list view, the same as iOS devices.
- The passcode icon tooltip now reads *Passcode enabled*.
- The *Passcode* filter in the device search bar now offers *Enabled* and *Not Enabled*. *Enabled* returns devices with a passcode on every platform.

For details, see xref:devices:device-metadata.adoc#_passcode[Passcode].

// Source: KOB-52746

=== Accurate memory values in Device Metrics

Device Metrics now shows the memory a device is actually using, matching Android Settings and Xcode Instruments, instead of reading 90%+.

* Android and iOS: memory the OS can reclaim on demand (cache) now counts as free.
* Sessions recorded before the upgrade keep their old, higher memory values.

// Source: KOB-52033

== Android device passcode fix

Fixed an issue where the *Passcode Feature Enforced* setting could turn off on its own for some Android devices. When this happened, a device that still had a passcode set could not be unlocked. The setting now stays on when an Android 8 or later device reconnects.

Android devices affected before this release may continue to show the setting off.

// Source: KOB-55544

=== Install `.app` files on real iOS devices during manual sessions

During a manual session on a real iOS device, *Upload File* and *Install From URL* in *Install Apps* now accept zipped `.app` files. A `.app` built for real iOS devices installs the same way as an `.ipa`.

Apps with a build type that doesn't match the device are now stopped before installation with a clear message, instead of failing with a generic install error:

* An iOS Simulator build is not installed on a real iOS device.
* A device build is not installed on an iOS Simulator.

Android sessions, and iOS apps whose build type matches the device, are unaffected.

For details, see xref:manual-testing:install-an-app.adoc#_ios_build_types[iOS build types].

// Source: KOB-53277

== Ended sessions no longer show as Running on the Sessions page

Sessions that have ended now keep their final status on the *Sessions* page, such as *Complete* or *Terminated*. This status matches the status shown on the session *Overview*.

Status and session details on the *Sessions* page also stay in sync more reliably when an update fails temporarily.

Sessions that already showed as *Running* after they ended, before this release, keep that status.

// Source: KOB-55807
// Release-note draft partial. Requires docs-team review before publication.

== Devices complete cleanup after sessions and reservations end

Fixed an issue where devices could remain in the *Awaiting cleanup configuration* status after a session ended or a reservation was canceled. Devices now complete cleanup as expected.

// Source: KOB-55657

=== First screenshots on Android devices

On Android devices, the first screenshot after a session starts, after the device rotates, or after the display refreshes now returns a valid image. This applies to the manual viewer, session video recording, and automation screenshots taken as the first command.

// Source: KOB-55737

== Check service status from the help widget

The help widget in Kobiton Portal now includes a *Kobiton Status Page* option, so you can check service status before contacting Support. The option appears after *Support* and opens https://status.kobiton.com/[status.kobiton.com^] in a new tab.

This option is available on Kobiton Public Cloud. Private Cloud and Standalone deployments are unchanged.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55737): The Jira release-note field also states that, on Standalone, the help widget and documentation pages no longer load Google Analytics. That change is omitted here because this entry covers the Public Cloud release. Confirm whether it belongs in the Standalone release notes.

// Source: KOB-55532

=== Reliable app lifecycle commands on iOS 15 and 16

On iOS 15 and iOS 16 devices, these commands stay reliable across long-running sessions and no longer require a device reboot to restore:

* CLI: `app run`, `app kill`, `device ps`
* Appium: `mobile: terminateApp`
